transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you and what brings you in today?

Hi, yeah. Thank you for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this, and I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. 

It's just... well, I'm a construction manager, so I'm on job sites all day. It's probably just a little stress or something, I really don't want to make a huge deal out of it, but... lately, every time I have to get near a scaffold, or, you know, a roof edge or an upper platform, my head just tells me I'm about to go over. 

And the thing is, I can literally see the rails are in place. I know the setup is supposed to be completely safe—I mean, it's my job to know that. But I still get this... this reaction. I'm sorry, does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you need to know?
Do you ever feel this same sense of fear or panic in situations that aren't related to heights or being on scaffolds or roofs?

No, no, not at all. It's really just the heights thing. I mean, I'm completely fine everywhere else—driving, being in crowds, small spaces, all of that is totally normal for me. I don't want you to think I'm, you know, falling apart or anything. I'm generally a very level-headed guy. It's just this one specific situation at work that's been... tricky. Is that helpful? I hope I'm answering your question right.
When you feel that fear near the scaffold or roof edge, do you notice any physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shaking?

Well, um... yeah, I guess I do get some of that. I mean, I really try to keep it under control, so it's not like I'm making a scene at work or anything. I don't want anyone to think I can't handle my job. 

But, honestly, the second I step onto temporary stairs, or... or even just walk toward an open upper floor, my chest gets really tight. And my hands get pretty sweaty, which is, you know, embarrassing. Sometimes I feel like my legs might just lock up completely before I can even make myself take another step. 

It's probably just a normal adrenaline thing, right? I mean, I hope that's not too extreme. Is that the kind of physical reaction you were asking about?
